title: Two Gaussians and a shared covariance
brief: Fit Gaussian discriminant analysis, show its posterior is exactly logistic regression, then build both flavours of naive Bayes.
hints: The pooled covariance is an MLE, so it divides by n, not by n - K. Accumulate the sum of (x_i - mean_k)(x_i - mean_k)^T over every point regardless of class, then divide once by n.

Use a Cholesky factor of the shared covariance to evaluate the Gaussian log-density: solve a triangular system for the Mahalanobis term instead of forming the inverse, and read the log-determinant off the diagonal of the factor.
gda_to_logistic only has to handle two classes. w = inv(cov) @ (means[1] - means[0]); b collects the two quadratic terms and the log prior ratio.
For the multinomial estimator, sum the count vectors of every document in a class before smoothing. Laplace smoothing adds alpha to every count and alpha * vocab_size to every denominator.
